package.author: Will Lehnertz

en-US.author: Will Lehnertz
en-US.longDescription:
Baudrun is a cross-platform (macOS + Windows + Linux) serial
terminal for network devices. Built for switch consoles, router
CLIs, and other serial-attached gear.

Profile-based: each device gets a named profile storing port,
baud rate, framing, flow control, line ending, and optional
send-on-connect sequences. One-click connect; no
`screen /dev/cu.usbserial-...` from memory.
en-US.name: Baudrun
en-US.releaseNotes:
Highlights
Fixed
- Tab reaches the device. Tab in the terminal now goes to the serial
  port, so tab completion works on Cisco and other consoles and in shells,
  instead of moving focus to the next control. Thanks to @leisiji (#135).
- x86_64 Linux packages start on Ubuntu 24.04 again. v0.17.0's .deb,
  .rpm and AppImage were built on Ubuntu 26.04 and failed with
  "GLIBC_2.43 not found" on older systems.
Changed
- Linux minimum is now Ubuntu 24.04, Debian 13 or Fedora 40. The
  packages need glibc 2.39; the old 22.04 / Debian 12 / Fedora 38 floor
  was already out of date.
What's Changed
- docs(changelog): add the Linux glibc fix to v0.17.1 (8700ab0)
- docs: raise the Linux minimum to Ubuntu 24.04 / Debian 13 / Fedora 40 (e0cc540)
- ci(release): build x86_64 Linux packages on Ubuntu 24.04 (b8ca043)
- docs(changelog): cut v0.17.1 — Tab reaches the device (5d8a78a)
- fix serial shell cannot receive tab (8a3344d)
- build(deps): Bump uuid from 1.29.0 to 1.29.1 in the cargo-minor group (294e191)
- build(deps): Bump the docs-minor group in /docs-next with 2 updates (0026087)
- build(deps): Bump the actions-all group with 3 updates (b83bc32)
Full Changelog: v0.17.0...v0.17.1
